chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about who is rejected among the witnesses. He said: 'The one suspected of bias, the accused, and the opposing party.' I said: 'The unrighteous (fasiq) and the treacherous?' He said: 'All of this falls under the category of the one suspected of bias.'

key_terms.اَلظَّنِينُ: The one suspected of bias or partiality
key_terms.اَلْفَاسِقُ: The unrighteous (one who commits sins openly)
key_terms.اَلْمُتَّهَمُ: The accused (of a defect or bias)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for rejecting a witness in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the jurisprudential principle of *al-zann* (suspected bias) as a comprehensive ground for witness disqualification. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that specific defects like being the opposing party (*al-khasm*) or unrighteous (*al-fasiq*) are subsumed under the broader category of *al-zannin*, ensuring judicial impartiality by excluding those with potential conflicts of interest or hidden flaws.
